social-b21e913de1bb.text: Some thoughts from that brutal #Giants loss to the #Commanders ... - The reason this one stings so bad for John Harbaugh, the players in the locker room is that it was theirs for the taking. So many opportunities from the first possession to the last flip the outcome. 1) Passing on the 55-yard field goal on the first possession. 2) Zvada missing the 33 yards. 3) The Malik Nabers fumble. 4) The Theo Johnson drop. 5) The failed Jameis sneak. 6) The QB power. The Commanders are a very flawed team, but you give a player like Jayden Daniels enough opportunities, and he's going to capitalize. - He's going to get ripped for those final two passes, the second of which to Malik Nabers was a legit 50/50 opportunity, but I thought J.J. McCarthy played a damn good game. He finished 23 of 36 for a career-high 293 yards, a TD, 34 yards on the ground. He's playing at such a high level. The layering of passes, the fastball when needed, his read progressions. It shows such promise. That throw to Isaiah Likely (the 66 yarder), which John Harbaugh called "crazy good," was a thing of beauty. A laser with a free rusher in his face between two defenders? Huge. As for the INT, and the near INT on the other play: Harbaugh said it was a cover zero blitz and those were the routes. McCarthy's arm was hit on both throws, but he said he was trying to give his playmakers a chance. Again: Nabers had a legit chance on second. He lost the 50/50 ball. One coach texted me while watching McCarthy play. He said, if this is the player the Giants have the rest of the season, "they're going to be a problem." - It sounds like Harbaugh is sticking with Dominic Zvada. OK, I guess. Doesn't seem that wise. He's missed six kicks since starting the season 9-for-9. Now the Giants don't trust him to attempt a 55 yarder? The league is nailing 60s like PATs. The miss from 33 in a game the Giants lost by three? This division is going to come down to the wire. The Giants aren't talented enough to blow teams out, especially the opponents awaiting them over the next month. You can't be giving possessions away as you wait for the rookie kicker to figure it out. A veteran should be in place this week to push Zvada in practice. Light a fire. - The loss will overshadow a damn good performance from Ar'Darius Washington. The safety, replacing Tyler Nubin (not good) and Jason Pinnock (back) singe handedly forced two turnover on downs. On one, he had a stick to bring up fourth down, then a pass breakup to give the Giants the ball back. On another, his tackle on Stefon Diggs on second down kept him short of the sticks. Two plays later, on fourth, he picked off Daniels. - How real/not real the Giants are is a hot topic because they haven't beaten a team with a winning record. They're about to get tested over their next four. The Giants will face the Jaguars (home), Colts (road), 49ers (home) and Seahawks (road). That's a gauntlet. Ideally, they find a way to be 2-2 out of it. Anything worse ... and the good feels after this strong start are over. That's kind of why this loss to the Commanders feels so gut wrenching. Not only was it there for New York, but a 6-2-1 mark reads so much better considering what lies ahead. - Updated NFC East standings: Giants (5-3-1), Cowboys (4-5), Commanders (3-5-1), Eagles (2-7). The Cowboys play the 49ers on Sunday. The Eagles are on their bye.
